title: Standby sentinel activation & liveness protocol for multi-region failover
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Redwood needs a robust, predictable way to activate warm standbys across regions that balances latency, cost-tier routing, and model-variant compatibility. Current probes are binary and can lead to noisy failovers or prolonged degraded routing. This ticket defines a sentinel-based liveness & activation protocol that primes KV caches, verifies model compatibility, and gates activation with quorum and latency budget checks.
background: We operate hosted clusters across multiple regions and offer tiered routing (premium/standard/burst). When a primary region degrades or an SLA-bound customer requires failover, we currently fail over based on simple health checks with limited cache priming. This causes increased tail latency and token cost during failover windows. Other recent work (ENG-62547, ENG-70321) focused on rebalancers and priming probes; this ticket builds a readable, auditable activation flow that coordinates with routing policies and fallback model variants.
proposal: Introduce a sentinel activation layer with the following characteristics: 1) Multi-step health scoring: Liveness, Latency P50/P95, Model-variant fingerprint match, KV prefix hit-rate estimate. 2) Quorum gating: activation requires agreement from region control-plane, at least two sentinel probes (controller+local agent), and an analytic sanity check (traffic simulation). 3) Latency-aware priming: selective KV cache priming on hot prefixes for top N customer routes and progressive traffic ramp to avoid cold-start spikes. 4) Cost-tier routing integration: when activating a standby for premium tier traffic prefer regions with reserved capacity; for standard/burst allow cheaper model variants with quality-steering thresholds. 5) Rollback hooks: immediate evacuate and failback if priming fails or latency exceeds budget during ramp. 6) Observability: per-activation audit log, priming progress metrics, and a post-activation health score computed over first 30 minutes.
implementation_plan: Phase A (infra and control-plane): add sentinel API in control-plane to request probe runs and commit activation; store activation metadata in activation ledger. Phase B (agents and priming): extend regional agents to run priming workloads, pre-warm KV caches for given prefixes, and validate model-variant checksums. Phase C (routing): extend smart-router to consult sentinel scores and to perform percentage-based ramping for traffic re-route. Phase D (safety): implement runtime circuit-breakers that can step-down activated region and route traffic to fallback variants with graceful degrade messaging.

acceptance_criteria: A control-plane API can request and persist a sentinel activation attempt
Regional agent performs selective KV cache priming for specified prefixes within configured time budgets
Activation only proceeds when sentinel health score >= 0.8 and quorum conditions satisfied
Smart-router can perform a progressive ramp (0% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) based on priming progress signals
If latency P95 exceeds configured SLA during ramp, traffic automatically reverts to previous routing within 60s
Post-activation audit log contains priming stats, model-variant checksums, and first-30min health-score
test_plan: Unit tests for sentinel API and health-score computation
Integration test: agent priming simulates hot prefixes and reports hit-rate back to control-plane
Chaos scenario: introduce synthetic packet loss in primary region and validate warm standby activation completes with ramp and rollback behavior
Performance test: measure token cost delta and P95 tail before/after activation under a 5k RPS synthetic workload
Regression test: model-variant mismatch should block activation and emit an alert
monitoring_and_alerting: New metric: sentinel.activation.attempts (labels: region, tier, initiator)
SLO alert: if post-activation health_score < 0.7 for > 5 minutes trigger oncall page
Cost alert: if priming increased egress/compute by > 150% of baseline over 10m, notify infra-cost team
Audit log retention: activation records retained for 90 days in egressed vault
dependencies: runtime-1.22: new kernel selection flags for priming workload
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: aggressive priming can oversubscribe GPU pools and push other customers into higher latency. Mitigation: priming budget per-region and backpressure signals from autoscaler; opt-in by customer tier for aggressive priming. Risk: model-variant fallback causes quality regressions. Mitigation: maintain a compatibility matrix with minimum evaluation thresholds; implement per-customer quality-rollback rules.
runbook_snippets: Activation steps (short): 1) Initiate sentinel activation; 2) Verify control-plane quorum; 3) Start selective KV priming (top N prefixes for affected customers); 4) Run synthetic traffic replay at 10% of target traffic; 5) If health_score stable, increment traffic to 25% and continue until 100% or abort; 6) Log activation metadata and notify SRE. Abort conditions: health_score drop > 0.15 within 5m, memory pressure > 85% on serving hosts, or model checksum mismatch.
